account: Today I have followed my appointments: market rounds, lunch at home, the accounts appointment, and tea with my neighbour. I have now returned to the office for the half-past-four appointment, a little late. The unusual thread is talk about supplies and lighting. My neighbour said the builder is arranging ordinary supplies and lighting for the town hall, and reported that Townsfolk Two had mentioned lights going up at the bakery. I have not personally confirmed the bakery lights or learned their purpose. I saw the builder carrying a lantern earlier; the builder and freight were with my neighbour at the inn, and I heard freight asking the innkeeper about a supply order. Those things could be connected, but I do not know that they are. The neighbour has repeatedly said there is no further confirmed news and cautioned against turning a passing report into a grand occasion. Tea itself was a quiet, friendly visit, with no revelation of any special event. The secretary had received no accounts or council papers for my thirteen-o'clock review and had no confirmed explanation of the hall arrangements. I asked the secretary to check directly with the builder. My suspicion is that preparations may be underway for some gathering or celebration, possibly involving the hall and bakery, but routine supplies and lighting remain an equally plausible explanation. I have no evidence yet of a secret plan or of anyone deliberately keeping me uninformed.
